back: The application for insurance, giving all material facts; the basis of the contract.
A temporary document giving cover until the policy is issued.
A booklet or web page describing an insurer's policies, cover, conditions and rates.
The formal contract: risks covered, sum insured, premium, period, conditions and exclusions.
Prospectus → proposal form → underwriting and premium → cover note → policy → renewal.
Report and notify → claim form with evidence → assessment by a loss adjuster → settlement (discharge form).
Broker: independent, many insurers, advises client. Agent: sells for one insurer.
Actuary calculates premium rates from statistics; underwriter decides on each individual risk and its premium.
Both investigate and value a loss: the adjuster acts for the insurer, the assessor for the insured.
